title: Abu al-Hasan and Abu Ja'afar the Leper

full_text:
Abu al-Hasan, a devout pilgrim traveling the road to Mecca, was walking through a desolate, rocky gorge in the heat of midday. Beside an overhanging rock sat an elderly man named Abu Ja'afar, who was afflicted with severe leprosy: his fingers were crippled, his eyesight was dim, and his flesh was covered in sores.

Yet as the traveler approached, he heard Abu Ja'afar reciting joyful praises with a voice full of vibrant sweetness: 'Praise be to the Merciful Creator, who has favored me above millions of His creatures, bestowing upon me endless blessings and radiant peace!'

Abu al-Hasan was filled with bewilderment. He halted his camel, knelt beside the invalid, and asked gently: 'O brother, may heaven comfort your afflictions! You sit alone in the scorching dust, crippled, blind, and sores cover your flesh. For what great blessings are you offering such joyful thanksgiving?'

Abu Ja'afar turned his sightless eyes toward the sky, smiled with radiant serenity, and replied: 'O traveler, look upon me! He has left me a heart that knows His love, and a tongue that can utter His praise! If all the kings of the earth were offered the treasure of my contented soul in exchange for their golden crowns, they would find my peace richer than all their empires. Shall I complain of a frail earthen vessel when the spirit within overflows with joy?'

Abu al-Hasan bowed his head to the dust, weeping with shame at his own past complaints over minor trials. He shared his waterskin and dates with Abu Ja'afar, prayed beside him, and continued his pilgrimage, having learned that true gratitude is a spiritual fortress that no physical affliction can conquer.
moral: Spiritual beauty and sincere gratitude shine brightest in bodies broken by affliction.
